codeSnippet:
# split a sentence into words
words = "a b c".____()

explanation.en: split() breaks a string on whitespace by default.

codeSnippet:
# total of a list of numbers
total = ____(nums)

explanation.en: sum() adds every item of an iterable.

codeSnippet:
# smallest value in the list
lowest = ____(nums)

explanation.en: min() returns the smallest element.

codeSnippet:
# does the name start with "Mr"?
flag = name.____("Mr")

explanation.en: startswith() tests a prefix and returns a boolean.

codeSnippet:
# drop surrounding whitespace
clean = raw.____()

explanation.en: strip() removes whitespace from both ends of a string.

codeSnippet:
# swap every comma for a space
out = text.____(",", " ")

explanation.en: replace(old, new) substitutes every occurrence.
push() appends to the end of an array.

codeSnippet:
// remove and return the FIRST item
const first = queue.____();

explanation.en: shift() removes the first element and returns it.

codeSnippet:
// is ANY score above 90?
const high = scores.____((s) => s > 90);

explanation.en: some() returns true when at least one element passes the test.

codeSnippet:
# True when EVERY value is positive
ok = ____(v > 0 for v in nums)

explanation.en: all() is True only when every item is truthy.

codeSnippet:
# True when AT LEAST ONE value is negative
bad = ____(v < 0 for v in nums)

explanation.en: any() is True as soon as one item is truthy.

codeSnippet:
// sum the array into one value
const total = nums.____((a, b) => a + b, 0);

explanation.en: reduce() folds an array down to a single value.
items() yields (key, value) tuples.

codeSnippet:
# longest word first
words.sort(____=len, reverse=True)

explanation.en: The key argument names the function used to rank each item.

codeSnippet:
# sort pairs by the second field
pairs.sort(key=____ p: p[1])

explanation.en: lambda builds a small anonymous function inline.
isinstance() checks a value against a type or tuple of types.

codeSnippet:
# add every item of another list
base.____(extra)

explanation.en: extend() appends each element, unlike append() which adds the list itself.

codeSnippet:
// map then flatten one level
const tags = posts.____((p) => p.tags);

explanation.en: flatMap() maps each item then flattens the result one level.

codeSnippet:
// always two digits: "7" -> "07"
const mm = String(m).____(2, '0');

explanation.en: padStart() pads the front until the string reaches the given length.

codeSnippet:
// a divider line of 20 dashes
const line = '-'.____(20);

explanation.en: repeat(n) returns the string joined to itself n times.

codeSnippet:
// remove 2 items starting at index 1
list.____(1, 2);

explanation.en: splice(start, count) removes items in place.

codeSnippet:
# how many times does 'a' appear?
n = letters.____("a")

explanation.en: count() returns the number of occurrences.

codeSnippet:
// parse a JSON string into an object
const cfg = JSON.____(raw);

explanation.en: JSON.parse() turns text into a value; stringify goes the other way.

codeSnippet:
// run no matter what happened above
try { save(); } catch (e) { log(e); } ____ { close(); }

explanation.en: finally runs whether or not an exception was thrown.
items() gives the pairs the comprehension swaps.
yield turns the function into a generator producing each running total.

codeSnippet:
// wait for every request together
const all = await Promise.____(ids.map(load));

explanation.en: Promise.all waits for every promise and keeps their order.

codeSnippet:
// first one to settle wins
const fastest = await Promise.____([a, b]);

explanation.en: Promise.race settles as soon as the first promise does.

codeSnippet:
# count each word in one line
from collections import Counter
tally = ____(words)

explanation.en: Counter builds a dict of element counts in one call.
